proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a raw atom \(A=\{V_{i,I}=y\}\).  Let \(I_{\leq i}\) be the restriction of \(I\) to coordinates at most \(i\).  By \texttt{def:ordered-evaluation}, an induction on \(t=1,\ldots,i\) gives
\[
 E(f,I)_t=E(f,I_{\leq i})_t,
\]
because the recursion at coordinate \(t\) consults only intervention entries at coordinates at most \(t\) and response values on coordinates strictly below \(t\).  Thus deleting entries with index greater than \(i\) leaves the truth value of \(A\) unchanged.  If \(i\in\operatorname{dom}(I)\), the same definition gives
\[
 E(f,I)_i=I(i),
 \qquad
 \mathbf 1\{V_{i,I}=y\}=\mathbf 1\{I(i)=y\},
\]
so the self-intervention replacement is also pointwise valid.  Otherwise all retained intervention coordinates precede \(i\).  Sorting their encodings and coalescing repeated identical pairs does not change the partial map \(I\), hence does not change \(E(f,I)_i\).  Boolean simplification of the resulting truth constants preserves the value of the conjunction.  Applying these facts to every atom yields, for every \(f\in\mathfrak F\) and \(j\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\),
\[
 \mathbf 1\{\gamma_j(f)\}
 =\mathbf 1\{\gamma_j^{\circ}(f)\}.
\]
Multiplication by \(c_j\) and summation therefore give
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^r c_j\mathbf 1\{\gamma_j(f)\}
 =\sum_{j=1}^r c_j\mathbf 1\{\gamma_j^{\circ}(f)\}=g(f).
\]

It remains to justify the preprocessing bound rather than assume it.  Scan the explicit token stream once, validate each coordinate and value against the explicitly listed alphabets charged in the definition of \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\), discard a later-coordinate pair as soon as its index is read, and perform a stable radix ordering of retained integer coordinate encodings.  The radix work is linear in the total number of bits in those encodings.  A second scan coalesces identical adjacent pairs and simplifies constants.  A deterministic binary trie on the normalized context encodings constructs the distinct set \(\mathcal H\), again in time linear in the number of input and output bits.  No step emits more tokens than it reads.  By the definition of \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\), the total time is therefore \(O(N_{\mathrm{in}})\).  The operations are prescribed in source order with canonical coordinate ordering, so \(\mathsf N\) is deterministic.  The retained atoms are predecessor-only, and the argument used only explicit unnested atoms; it makes no claim about succinct nested syntax.

Let \(\mathcal M\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ord}}\).  For each \(u\in\mathcal U\), define \(f^u\) as in the frozen symbol declaration:
\[
 f_i^u(x_{<i})=\varphi_i(x_{\operatorname{pa}_i},u).
\]
Order compatibility in \texttt{ass:order-compatible-parent-sets} makes the right-hand side well typed, and \texttt{ass:complete-predecessor-functions} implies \(f^u\in\mathfrak F\); the coordinates outside \(\operatorname{pa}_i\) are simply ignored.  Put \(\Psi(u)=f^u\) and define the push-forward law
\[
 \mu(f)=\nu\bigl(\Psi^{-1}(\{f\})\bigr),\qquad f\in\mathfrak F.
\]
The carrier \(\mathfrak F\) is finite by \texttt{ass:finite-alphabets}.  The displayed preimages are measurable events of the finite-valued structural equations in the standard SCM of \texttt{def:ordered-scm-class}; they partition \(\mathcal U\).  Hence
\[
 \mu(f)\geq0,qquad
 \sum_{f\in\mathfrak F}\mu(f)
 =\nu(\mathcal U)=1,
\]
and the image lies in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{can}}\) by \texttt{def:canonical-carrier-class}.

For every valid intervention \(I\), induction in the causal order proves equality of the original and canonical evaluations.  Indeed, if coordinate \(i\) is intervened, both values equal \(I(i)\).  Otherwise, assuming equality below \(i\),
\[
 E(f^u,I)_i
 =f_i^u(E(f^u,I)_{<i})
 =\varphi_i(E(f^u,I)_{\operatorname{pa}_i},u)
 =\varphi_i(V^I_{\operatorname{pa}_i}(u),u)
 =V_i^I(u).
\]
Thus every factual or intervention-world vector agrees pointwise.  Every explicit unnested conjunction, and consequently every score \(g\), is a finite Boolean function of those vectors, so
\[
 g(f^u)=g_{\mathcal M}(u),qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mu}[g(f)]
 =\sum_{f\in\mathfrak F}\nu(\Psi^{-1}(\{f\}))g(f)
 =\mathbb E_{\nu}[g(f^U)].
\]
Taking \(I=\varnothing\) proves preservation of the observational law as well.

Conversely, take \((k,(\mathcal D_i),\mathfrak F,\mu)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{can}}\), set \(\mathcal U=\mathfrak F\), \(\nu=\mu\),
\[
 \operatorname{pa}_i=\{1,\ldots,i-1\},
 \qquad
 \varphi_i(x_{<i},f)=f_i(x_{<i}),
\]
and use the shared exogenous variable \(U=f\).  These parent sets satisfy \texttt{ass:order-compatible-parent-sets}, and ordered evaluation is exactly \(E(f,I)\).  This constructs a member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ord}}\) with the same observational and counterfactual laws.  The two maps therefore preserve compatibility with each supplied \(p\) and preserve \(\theta_g\) in both directions.  Their compatible attainable sets, and hence every minimum and maximum over those sets, are identical.  This direct argument establishes the compiler interface that the statement attributes to Rossetto--Antonucci; the attribution is not used as an unproved premise.

The assertion is vacuous for continuation when \(i=k\), so first take \(i<k\) and write \(q=i+1\).  Let a feasible partial evaluation have partition \(\pi_i\).  For a block \(T\in\pi_i\), split its worlds into
\[
 N_T=\{w\in T:q\notin\operatorname{dom}(w)\},
 \qquad
 J_T=T\setminus N_T.
\]
Here a context \(w\) is identified with its intervention.  By \texttt{def:prefix-partition}, all worlds in \(T\) have the same complete predecessor tuple \(x^w_{<q}\).  Consequently, \texttt{def:ordered-evaluation} forces one common value \(z_T\in\mathcal D_q\) on every world in \(N_T\), while each \(w\in J_T\) has the fixed value \(w(q)\).  Conversely, different blocks of \(\pi_i\) have different complete predecessor tuples, so \texttt{ass:complete-predecessor-functions} permits their values \(z_T\) to be selected independently.

It follows that a column \(y=(y_w)_{w\in\mathcal H}\) is legal at coordinate \(q\) exactly when
\[
 y_w=w(q)\quad(w\in J_T),
 \qquad
 y_w=z_T\quad(w\in N_T)
\]
for some \(z_T\in\mathcal D_q\) for every block \(T\), and when the entries of \(y\) obey the factual and normalized-query pins at coordinate \(q\).  These conditions mention the preceding history only through \(\pi_i\).  Given such a column, define the row of \(f_q\) at the predecessor tuple belonging to \(T\) to be \(z_T\).  The tuples for distinct blocks are distinct, so these assignments are consistent; finiteness and nonemptiness in \texttt{ass:finite-alphabets} allow arbitrary default values on all unlisted tuples.  Therefore every legal column is realizable.

Now take two feasible histories with the same \(\pi_i\).  The preceding characterization gives them the same set of legal numeric columns.  Appending the same column splits each old block according to equality of its new entries, and blocks that were already distinct cannot merge because their complete prefixes remain unequal.  Hence the two histories induce the same \(\pi_{i+1}\).  Induction on \(q=i+1,\ldots,k\) gives identical supports of all later column sequences subject to all later pins.  This proves both inclusions of the asserted continuation-support equality.

For an accepted transition path, at coordinate \(q\) record one pair
\[
 (x^w_{<q},z_T)
\]
for each block \(T\) containing at least one natural world, choosing any such \(w\in N_T\).  There are at most \(h\) recorded pairs per coordinate and hence at most \(kh\) in total.  If the same predecessor tuple occurs for two natural worlds, those worlds are in the same block and the transition rule assigned the same output, so the recorded rows are consistent.  Choose a default \(d_q\in\mathcal D_q\), which exists by \texttt{ass:finite-alphabets}, and assign it to every unlisted tuple as in \texttt{def:sparse-response-completion}.  Induction over coordinates then shows that the completed \(\widehat f\) reproduces every stored world column: intervened coordinates use their constants, and natural coordinates find precisely their recorded row.  Thus \(\widehat f\in\mathfrak F\), proving the stated sparse-extension claim as well as realizability of every representative path.

First consider one normalized conjunction and a block \(T\in\pi_i\) at coordinate \(q=i+1\).  All natural worlds in \(T\) call the same row by \texttt{thm:partition-continuation}.  If there is no natural world, the column on \(T\) is fixed by interventions.  If natural pins disagree, no output can meet them.  If they agree on a value, there is one possible natural output.  In the remaining case let \(C_T\) be the set of distinct intervention constants in \(T\).  For \(z,z'\in\mathcal D_q\setminus C_T\), the natural worlds form one new subblock, separate from every intervention-constant subblock, under either choice.  Thus \(z\) and \(z'\) give the same refinement and violate no natural pin.  The exact-continuation theorem gives the same future support.  A choice \(z\in C_T\), by contrast, merges the natural subblock with the worlds carrying that particular constant and is therefore retained separately.  This proves soundness and completeness of \(\mathsf C_1\)'s representative list, including the case \(\mathcal D_q\setminus C_T=\varnothing\).

For the count, let a branching block have \(a\) intervened and \(b\geq1\) natural worlds, and put \(t=a+b\).  It has at most \(a+1\leq t\) representatives.  For integers \(t=1,2,3\), direct calculation gives \(t\leq3^{t/3}\).  For \(t\geq3\), the derivative of \(x\mapsto \log(x)/x\) is \((1-\log x)/x^2<0\), whence
\[
 \frac{\log t}{t}\leq\frac{\log3}{3},
 \qquad t\leq3^{t/3}.
\]
The block containing the factual world is nonbranching because that natural output is pinned by \(v\).  If \(t_1,\ldots,t_m\) are the sizes of all branching blocks, then \(\sum_jt_j\leq h-1\), and therefore
\[
 \prod_{j=1}^m t_j
 \leq3^{\sum_jt_j/3}
 \leq3^{(h-1)/3}.
\]

For the joint compiler, attach a flag vector \(a_i\in\{0,1\}^r\) to the partition.  Before branching at coordinate \(q\), coalesce repeated identical tests.  If a live term tests two distinct constants at the same world-coordinate, that term necessarily fails at this coordinate, so set its flag to zero before forming representatives.  This is a value-preserving Boolean simplification, including the contradictory/repeated-term case; afterward each live term tests at most one constant per world at coordinate \(q\).

For an unpinned natural group in \(T\), let \(C_T\) now contain the distinct intervention constants and the constants tested on natural worlds by live terms.  Two outputs outside \(C_T\) have the same equality relation to every intervention constant and fail exactly the same current tests.  They consequently give the same refined partition and the same updated flag vector; \texttt{thm:partition-continuation} then gives the same future support.  Retaining every member of \(C_T\cap\mathcal D_q\) and one member of \(\mathcal D_q\setminus C_T\), when nonempty, is therefore both sound and complete.

If \(T\) contains \(a\) intervened and \(b\geq1\) natural worlds, there are at most \(a+rb+1\) representatives.  Since \(r\geq1\) and \(t=a+b\),
\[
 a+rb+1\leq rt+1\leq(r+1)^t,
\]
where the last inequality follows by retaining the first two terms in the binomial expansion of \((1+r)^t\).  Again the factual block is nonbranching, so multiplication over branching blocks gives
\[
 \prod_T(r+1)^{|T|}
 \leq(r+1)^{h-1}.
\]
The update rule is conjunction with precisely the tests at the new coordinate, so a dead flag needs no further information and a live flag records exactly that all processed tests passed.  Thus equality of the partition and flags is a right congruence for future transitions.  This proves the claimed joint soundness, completeness, and transition bound.

By \texttt{lem:query-normalization}, computing \(\gamma^{\circ}=\mathsf N(\gamma)\) preserves its truth for every \(f\) and costs \(O(N_{\mathrm{in}})\).  Under the stated convention \(r=1\), \(c_1=1\), the definition of \(A_v\) gives
\[
 A_v=\{(g_{\gamma^{\circ}}(f)):f\in F_v\}\subseteq\{0,1\},
\]
and hence, by \texttt{def:cell-labels},
\[
 \ell_g(v)=\min_{f\in F_v}g_{\gamma^{\circ}}(f),
 \qquad
 u_g(v)=\max_{f\in F_v}g_{\gamma^{\circ}}(f).
\]
Every \(F_v\) is nonempty: set \(f_i(v_{<i})=v_i\) for every \(i\) and extend all other rows by arbitrary values from the nonempty alphabets.

The dynamic program starts at \(\pi_0=\{\mathcal H\}\), applies \(\mathsf C_1\)'s representative transitions, and merges equal successor partitions.  By \texttt{lem:representative-transition} and induction over the coordinates, its states are exactly the partitions having a feasible partial response system satisfying all pins processed so far.  Thus it has an accepting terminal state if and only if some \(f\in F_v\) satisfies \(\gamma^{\circ}\).  A predecessor pointer and selected representative column on the first edge entering each state recover an accepting path.  At each coordinate, record the selected output once for every distinct natural predecessor tuple encountered on that path.  Soundness of the transition rule makes repeated rows consistent, there are at most \(h\) rows per coordinate, and assigning an arbitrary alphabet default on every unlisted tuple produces \(\widehat f\in\mathfrak F\).  Ordered induction shows that it reproduces the stored columns.  Thus the witness has at most \(kh\) stored rows and one default per coordinate.

There are at most \(B_h\) partitions at a layer, at most \(3^{(h-1)/3}\) representative column choices from each state, and \(k\), alphabet scans, pin checks, canonical partition encoding, and traceback are polynomial in \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\).  Therefore the decision and witness time is
\[
 B_h3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}).
\]

For completeness, we derive the false bit rather than infer it from failure of separate atom tests.  Let \(A=\{V_{i,I}=y\}\) be a retained atom, so \(i\notin\operatorname{dom}(I)\) and every intervention coordinate precedes \(i\).  Then
\[
 \bigl(\forall f\in F_v:\ E(f,I)_i=y\bigr)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 |\mathcal D_i|=1
 \ \text{or}\ 
 \bigl(I(t)=v_t\text{ for all }t\in\operatorname{dom}(I)\text{ and }v_i=y\bigr).
\]
If \(|\mathcal D_i|=1\), validity of the input forces \(y\) to be its sole value.  If \(I\) agrees with \(v\), induction below \(i\) using \texttt{def:ordered-evaluation} gives \(E(f,I)_{<i}=v_{<i}\) for every \(f\in F_v\), and therefore \(E(f,I)_i=f_i(v_{<i})=v_i\).  These prove the reverse implication and the agreeing case.

For the remaining direction, suppose \(|\mathcal D_i|>1\).  If \(I\) agrees with \(v\) but \(v_i\neq y\), every member of \(F_v\) falsifies the atom.  If \(I\) disagrees with \(v\), its first disagreeing intervention coordinate makes \(E(f,I)_{<i}\neq v_{<i}\), irrespective of later choices.  Select \(z\in\mathcal D_i\setminus\{y\}\), prescribe the factual rows \(f_t(v_{<t})=v_t\), prescribe arbitrary consistent rows along the \(I\)-world through coordinate \(i-1\), and set
\[
 f_i(E(f,I)_{<i})=z,
 \qquad
 f_i(v_{<i})=v_i.
\]
The two arguments are distinct, so these prescriptions are consistent, and sparse-response completion extends them to an \(f\in F_v\) falsifying the atom.  The displayed equivalence follows.

A false truth constant from normalization makes the whole conjunction identically false.  Otherwise, if every retained atom satisfies the right-hand side of the equivalence, all are true for every \(f\in F_v\), so \(\ell_g(v)=1\).  If at least one does not, the construction for that one supplies an \(f\in F_v\) that falsifies the conjunction, so \(\ell_g(v)=0\).  Thus a single linear scan computes the false bit; it does not require one response system that falsifies all atoms.  The empty conjunction has both labels one.  The true bit is exactly the accepting-state decision already proved.

It remains to relate the cell calculations to the causal target.  For any compatible canonical law \(\mu\), observational compatibility and the partition of \(\mathfrak F\) into the fibres \(F_v\) give
\[
 \theta_g
 =\sum_{v\in\mathcal X}\sum_{f\in F_v}\mu(f)g(f),
 \qquad
 \sum_{f\in F_v}\mu(f)=p(v).
\]
Since \(\ell_g(v)\leq g(f)\leq u_g(v)\) on \(F_v\), multiplication by \(\mu(f)\geq0\) and summation yield
\[
 L_g(p)=\sum_vp(v)\ell_g(v)
 \leq\theta_g\leq
 \sum_vp(v)u_g(v)=U_g(p).
\]
For each positive-mass cell choose a minimizing, respectively maximizing, response system supplied by the preceding constructions, and put exogenous mass \(p(v)\) on that system.  Its factual law is \(p\), and its expected score is exactly the corresponding endpoint.  Zero-mass cells require no choice.  Convexly mixing the two compatible endpoint laws preserves \(p\) and fills the interval.  By \texttt{prop:canonical-carrier-equivalence}, the same sharp interval holds over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ord}}\).  The Rossetto--Antonucci comparison in the statement is extensional: their named order-only cell extrema and the displayed extrema optimize the same response fibres after this canonical equivalence, so their endpoint values coincide; no additional identifying premise is used.  The construction above never enumerates a completed response signature: its only exponential state and transition factors are \(B_h\) and \(3^{(h-1)/3}\), while every alphabet operation is a charged polynomial scan.  It is therefore the stated \(h\)-parameter replacement of the completed-signature alphabet-product quotient on the same cells.

For sparse input, running the cell procedure only on the \(s\) listed positive-mass cells costs
\[
 sB_h3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}),
\]
in addition to the already charged input scan.  For dense input, reading all supplied cells is itself included in \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\).  This proves the claimed representation-sensitive runtime without treating an unobserved sample cell as a structural zero.

Normalize first.  By \texttt{lem:query-normalization}, this costs \(O(N_{\mathrm{in}})\) and leaves every term truth value, hence \(g(f)\), unchanged.  At layer \(i\), initialize or update a flag \(a_{i,j}\) so that
\[
 a_{i,j}=1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{every normalized atom of \(\gamma_j^{\circ}\) at a coordinate at most \(i\) is true}.
\]
An empty conjunction starts at one, and an identically false normalized term starts at zero.  The update is Boolean conjunction with all tests at coordinate \(i+1\), so a zero flag remains zero.

We prove by induction on \(i\) that the reachable states \((\pi_i,a_i)\) are exactly the partition-and-partial-truth pairs induced by feasible partial response systems in \(F_v\).  This is true at \(i=0\).  Given the claim at \(i\), \texttt{lem:representative-transition} states that every concrete legal column has a representative with the same successor partition and flags, and that every representative is realizable.  The two directions establish the induction step.  If two concrete histories merge into the same state, \texttt{thm:partition-continuation} gives them identical future column support, while equality of flags gives identical truth status for all already processed atoms.  Hence the merge loses neither a terminal truth vector nor a witness.  At \(i=k\), all atoms have been processed, so
\[
 \{a_k:(\pi_k,a_k)\text{ is reachable for some }\pi_k\}
 =A_v.
\]

There are at most \(B_h2^r\) states at any layer.  From each state, the joint representative lemma gives at most \((r+1)^{h-1}\) column choices.  Coordinate processing, normalized-test updates, canonicalization, rational score comparison, and all alphabet scans have bit complexity polynomial in \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\).  Thus the total time is
\[
 B_h2^r(r+1)^{h-1}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}).
\]
Store, for the first occurrence of each state, its predecessor and selected concrete representative column.  Backtracking from one terminal state for each reachable \(a\), followed by \texttt{def:sparse-response-completion} and \texttt{thm:partition-continuation}, returns a complete sparse witness for that truth vector.  Scanning the exact finite set \(A_v\) then computes
\[
 \ell_g(v)=\min_{a\in A_v}c^\top a,
 \qquad
 u_g(v)=\max_{a\in A_v}c^\top a.
\]

For soundness of the advertised identified set, let \(\mu\) be any canonical law compatible with \(p\).  The factual fibres are disjoint and exhaust \(\mathfrak F\), and \texttt{ass:observational-compatibility} gives their masses.  Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_g
 &=\sum_{v\in\mathcal X}\sum_{f\in F_v}\mu(f)g(f),\\
 \sum_{f\in F_v}\mu(f)&=p(v),\\
 \ell_g(v)&\leq g(f)\leq u_g(v)\qquad(f\in F_v).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Nonnegativity of \(\mu\) now gives
\[
 L_g(p)\leq\theta_g\leq U_g(p).
\]
The derivation optimizes \(c^\top a\) over the joint set \(A_v\); replacing it by separate marginal optimizations would enlarge the feasible set from \(A_v\) to a Cartesian product and is not licensed by any step.

The bounds are attained.  Because \(F_v\neq\varnothing\) and is finite, choose compiler witnesses \(f_v^-\) and \(f_v^+\) attaining \(\ell_g(v)\) and \(u_g(v)\) for each \(v\) with \(p(v)>0\).  Define shared-exogenous laws with one positive-mass atom per such cell by
\[
 \mu^-(f_v^-)=p(v),
 \qquad
 \mu^+(f_v^+)=p(v).
\]
Response systems belonging to different factual fibres are distinct, so these assignments are unambiguous; their masses sum to one by \texttt{ass:shared-exogenous-law}.  Their factual laws are \(p\), and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mu^-}[g(f)]=\sum_vp(v)\ell_g(v)=L_g(p),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mu^+}[g(f)]=\sum_vp(v)u_g(v)=U_g(p).
\]
For \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), the mixture \((1-\lambda)\mu^-+\lambda\mu^+\) remains compatible with \(p\) and has score \((1-\lambda)L_g(p)+\lambda U_g(p)\).  Hence the canonical identified set is exactly the full interval.  Finally, \texttt{prop:canonical-carrier-equivalence} transfers both inclusions and all attaining models to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ord}}\), proving
\[
 \Theta_g(p)=[L_g(p),U_g(p)].
\]

The first sentence is an induction directly from \texttt{def:numeric-history-baseline}.  Initially the unique empty history is feasible.  If the invariant holds after coordinate \(i\), the baseline expands every feasible numeric next column and discards exactly those successors violating a pin encountered at coordinate \(i+1\).  It therefore retains every and only feasible pinned history at the next layer.  Its merge rule identifies two paths only when all stored numeric prefixes and their flags coincide, so distinct feasible histories are never merged.

Now fix \(n\geq1\) in \texttt{def:separation-family}.  Write the worlds as \(0=\varnothing\), \(A\), and \(B\).  After \(S,T\), their prefixes are respectively
\[
 (0,0),\qquad(1,0),\qquad(1,1).
\]
Indeed, the factual cell pins the first pair to \((0,0)\), both intervention worlds set \(S=1\), the atom \(T_A=0\) pins the natural \(A\)-row, and \(B\) intervenes to set \(T=1\).  These three complete prefixes are pairwise distinct.

For an arbitrary \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in\{0,1\}^n\), prescribe at coordinate \(X_i\)
\[
 X_{i,0}=0,
 \qquad
 X_{i,A}=0,
 \qquad
 X_{i,B}=a_i.
\]
At every such coordinate, the three worlds present pairwise distinct complete predecessor tuples because a difference already occurred in \((S,T)\).  The complete-predecessor assumption therefore permits the three natural response rows to be assigned independently.  Induction over \(i\) realizes all the displayed values without conflict.  At \(Y\), the factual predecessor tuple and the \(B\)-world predecessor tuple are still distinct, so assign
\[
 Y_0=0,qquad Y_B=1,
\]
and choose the unused \(A\)-row arbitrarily.  Sparse completion yields a member of \(\mathfrak F\).  Thus every \(a\) gives a feasible pre-\(Y\) history satisfying every pin already encountered and having an accepting completion.

Conversely, all entries of such a pinned pre-\(Y\) history except \((X_{1,B},\ldots,X_{n,B})\) are fixed by the factual cell, interventions, and conjunction, and this remaining vector is binary.  Hence there are at most \(2^n\) histories.  The construction supplies all of them, and distinct vectors give distinct stored numeric histories.  The baseline invariant and its no-merge rule therefore give
\[
 N_{\mathrm{num}}(n)=2^n.
\]

Since complete prefixes never become equal after they differ, every one of these histories has the same three-singleton partition from the layer after \(T\) through the pre-\(Y\) layer.  In \(\mathsf C_1\), the factual and \(A\)-world outputs at each \(X_i\) are pinned to zero.  The unpinned singleton \(B\)-block has no intervention constant there, so all of its alphabet values induce the same singleton refinement and one fresh representative suffices.  Consequently there is one accepting partition state at each such layer, and the terminal pin \(Y_B=1\) is feasible.  This proves the stated separation from the explicitly path-retaining \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{num}}\).  Nothing in the argument applies a lower bound to an arbitrary reduced decision diagram or another compilation language.

theorem.statement: With the convention \(\operatorname{Bell}(0)=1\), the residual-state complexity is \(\rho(h)=\operatorname{Bell}(h-1)\) for every \(h\geq1\).  More precisely, for a fixed factual cell \(v\) and layer \(i\), the block of \(\pi_i\) containing the factual context is determined by \(v\) and \(\mathcal H\); restricting \(\pi_i\) to the remaining contexts is therefore an exact state and gives at most \(\operatorname{Bell}(h-1)\) states.  The single-conjunction compiler \(\mathsf C_1\) consequently runs in \(\operatorname{Bell}(h-1)3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})\) time.  Conversely, for every \(h\), one binary instance on the complete-predecessor carrier \(\mathfrak F\) and one factual cell have \(\operatorname{Bell}(h-1)\) reachable prefix partitions that are pairwise distinguished under the residual equivalence by legal terminal normalized conjunctions \(\gamma^{\circ}\).  This is a state-count lower bound, not an \(h\log h\) time lower bound.
theorem.proof_tex:
Fix a cell \(v\) and a layer \(i\).  For a context \(w\in\mathcal H\), define
\[
 A_i(v)=\bigl\{w\in\mathcal H:
 w(t)=v_t\text{ for every }t\leq i\text{ in }\operatorname{dom}(w)\bigr\}.
\]
The factual context belongs to \(A_i(v)\), so this set is nonempty.  We claim that it is exactly the block of \(\pi_i\) containing the factual context, for every feasible prefix in \(F_v\).  If \(w\in A_i(v)\), induction on \(t\leq i\) gives \(E(f,w)_t=v_t\): an intervened coordinate equals \(v_t\) by definition of \(A_i(v)\), while a natural coordinate sees the factual predecessor tuple and hence equals \(f_t(v_{<t})=v_t\).  If \(w\notin A_i(v)\), at its first disagreeing intervened coordinate \(t\leq i\),
\[
 E(f,w)_t=w(t)\neq v_t=E(f,\varnothing)_t,
\]
so its complete prefix is not factual.  This proves the claim.

The set \(A_i(v)\) is computable from the input and the cell and does not depend on the partial response rows.  Every reachable \(\pi_i\) is consequently reconstructed from its restriction to \(\mathcal H\setminus A_i(v)\) by adjoining the single known block \(A_i(v)\).  Since \texttt{thm:partition-continuation} uses only the reconstructed partition, this restriction is an exact continuation state.  The number of such restricted partitions is at most
\[
 \operatorname{Bell}(|\mathcal H\setminus A_i(v)|)
 \leq\operatorname{Bell}(h-1).
\]
The inequality is elementary: extend any partition of a set of size at most \(h-1\) to a partition of an \((h-1)\)-element set by adjoining each new element as a singleton; this is an injection.
Replacing the \(B_h\) state count in the proof of \texttt{thm:single-conjunction-compiler} by this bound, while leaving its representative-transition bound unchanged, gives
\[
 \operatorname{Bell}(h-1)3^{(h-1)/3}
 \operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}).
\]

We prove that no uniformly smaller exact residual state space is possible.  Put \(m=h-1\), label the nonfactual contexts by \(J=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and use binary variables ordered as
\[
 S\prec (Z_C)_{\varnothing\neq C\subsetneq J}\prec Y,
\]
in any fixed order among the \(Z_C\)'s.  When \(m\leq1\), the middle family is empty.  Let the factual cell be zero.  For \(j\in J\), define a context \(I_j\) by
\[
 I_j(S)=1,
 \qquad
 I_j(Z_C)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad j\in C,
\]
with no other interventions.  The contexts are distinct, and together with \(\varnothing\) form a set of size \(h\).  After \(S\), the factual world is a singleton block and all contexts \(I_j\) share the prefix \((1)\).

Let \(\tau\) be any partition of \(J\).  We construct response rows whose partition after the last \(Z_C\) is
\[
 \{\{\varnothing\}\}\cup\tau.
\]
At the coordinate \(Z_C\), assign zero to the factual row.  On each currently natural nonfactual predecessor tuple, assign zero if \(C\) is a block of \(\tau\), and assign one otherwise.  If \(C\) is not a block of \(\tau\), all intervened worlds and all natural worlds in any current nonfactual block then append one, so no such block splits.  If \(C\) is a block of \(\tau\), the worlds in \(C\) append the intervention value one and all other natural nonfactual worlds append zero; thus \(C\) is split from any current block containing it.  Previously separated blocks never merge.  After the coordinates indexed by all blocks of \(\tau\) have appeared, and hence at the end of the middle family, the partition is exactly \(\{\{\varnothing\}\}\cup\tau\).  Distinct current blocks call distinct complete-predecessor rows, so every prescription is consistent and extends by defaults.  Thus all \(\operatorname{Bell}(m)\) such partitions are reachable in the same context system and factual cell.

Finally take distinct partitions \(\tau\) and \(\sigma\) of \(J\).  There is an orientation \((\alpha,\beta)\) of this pair and a map \(q:J\to\{0,1\}\) that is constant on every block of \(\alpha\) but nonconstant on some block of \(\beta\).  To see this, if \(\beta\) is not a refinement of \(\alpha\), choose a \(\beta\)-block meeting two \(\alpha\)-blocks and assign different binary values to those two \(\alpha\)-blocks; if \(\beta\) is a proper refinement of \(\alpha\), reverse their roles.  Set \(q(\varnothing)=0\) and use the predecessor-normal terminal conjunction
\[
 \gamma_q^{\circ}
 =\{Y_{\varnothing}=0\}
 \wedge\bigwedge_{j\in J}\{Y_{I_j}=q(j)\}.
\]
All its contexts occur explicitly and none intervenes on \(Y\).  From the prefix with partition \(\{\{\varnothing\}\}\cup\alpha\), assign the natural \(Y\)-row of each block its common required value, so the conjunction is feasible.  From the prefix with partition \(\{\{\varnothing\}\}\cup\beta\), two worlds in one block require different values, but they call the same \(Y\)-row, so the conjunction is infeasible.  Hence the \(\operatorname{Bell}(m)\) reachable prefixes are pairwise distinct residuals under \texttt{def:residual-minimality-handle}.  Combining this lower bound with the preceding upper bound proves \(\rho(h)=\operatorname{Bell}(h-1)\), including \(h=1\), where the complement of the factual block is empty and has one partition.  The argument counts necessary exact states only and makes no assertion that an implementation must spend time proportional to their explicit enumeration.
theorem.justification: The factual cell makes one partition block deterministic, and the remaining context partitions are both sufficient and jointly realizable in the worst case.
theorem.gap: This resolves the causal residual count without promoting a state lower bound into a time lower bound.
theorem.consumer: The single-conjunction compiler may replace its Bell number state factor by the exact one-smaller-context Bell number.
